title: Farm Solar Array: irradiance sensor fault (2018-01-17 to 2018-01-22)
summary: Irradiance sensor fault detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 6 day(s), 2018-01-17 to 2018-01-22.
evidence: The sunlight sensor reported for only 7% of the time the site was producing power.
The site produced power but the irradiance sensor reported nothing.
recommended_actions: Clean the plane-of-array pyranometer and check its level and tilt alignment
Cross-check its readings against a second on-site sensor or satellite irradiance
Recalibrate or replace the sensor if the offset persists
Treat performance numbers for this window as unreliable until fixed
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: partial outage (2018-04-05 to 2018-04-07)

evidence: The site produced 99% of its expected output in the two weeks before, and 72% during this problem (100% = producing what the weather allows).
About 2,107 kWh lost (34% of what was expected over these days), worth roughly $253 at $0.12/kWh.
The size of the drop suggests roughly 33% of the array went offline.
Performance stepped down abruptly and stayed flat, the signature of a share of the array going offline (an inverter, a combiner or a string).
likely_causes: One inverter or inverter module offline
Tripped DC disconnect in one block
recommended_actions: Compare inverter- and combiner-level currents to locate the offline section
Pull inverter fault logs for the start date
Inspect combiner-box fuses and string connectors in the affected block
Run IV-curve traces on suspect strings; replace failed fuses or components
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

About 2,767 kWh lost (13% of what was expected over these days), worth roughly $332 at $0.12/kWh.
The slide seems to have started around 2023-05-24, 6 days before it was big enough to raise an alert.
In the week after, output recovered to 94% of the site's normal level.
A slow, steady slide in performance with no sudden step, the signature of dust or pollen build-up (or gradual degradation).
likely_causes: Dust or pollen build-up during a dry spell
recommended_actions: Visually inspect a sample of modules and photograph the soiling
Compare against the decline start date and the last rain or wash
Schedule a wash if the recoverable energy outweighs the cleaning cost; check the rain forecast first
After cleaning, confirm the performance index returns to its baseline
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: partial outage (2023-06-07 to 2023-06-09)

About 2,520 kWh lost (17% of what was expected over these days), worth roughly $302 at $0.12/kWh.
The size of the drop suggests roughly 16% of the array went offline.
Performance stepped down abruptly and stayed flat, the signature of a share of the array going offline (an inverter, a combiner or a string).
likely_causes: One inverter or inverter module offline
Tripped DC disconnect in one block
recommended_actions: Compare inverter- and combiner-level currents to locate the offline section
Pull inverter fault logs for the start date
Inspect combiner-box fuses and string connectors in the affected block
Run IV-curve traces on suspect strings; replace failed fuses or components
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: irradiance sensor fault (2023-11-02 to 2023-11-09)
summary: Irradiance sensor fault detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 8 day(s), 2023-11-02 to 2023-11-09.
evidence: The sunlight sensor reported for only 0% of the time the site was producing power.
The site produced power but the irradiance sensor reported nothing.
recommended_actions: Clean the plane-of-array pyranometer and check its level and tilt alignment
Cross-check its readings against a second on-site sensor or satellite irradiance
Recalibrate or replace the sensor if the offset persists
Treat performance numbers for this window as unreliable until fixed
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.
